Three Times is Still a Charm at La Villa
Feb 2024 • Couples
Three Times is Still a Charm

After we booked our Southeast Asian cruise, we knew we wanted to go back to the La Villa French restaurant that we found in 2012. At that time the La Villa was a newer French restaurant located in a developing district of Ho Chi Minh City. Thierry and Tina are excellent hosts and are fully deserving of their accolades. The service you receive is second to none. You can read my first review of La Villa in Tripadvisor, dated 12/2/2012. On this occasion, we ordered the Set Menu #2. The food and presentation were excellent. We dined with another couple who never experienced La Villa but who were familiar with French cuisine having lived many years in Provence. They too were impressed. I highly recommend La Villa for travelers and residents alike. For cruisers, it’s a 20 min ride from Ben Thanh market but could be hard to find. Just use a metered taxi and follow your progress on a Maps navigation app. From Ben Thanh, it’s less than 300 baht and La Villa will call a taxi for you after your meal. One final note. We made our reservation many weeks out and La Villa asked for a deposit. That seemed reasonable since La Villa is a small restaurant with a limited number of tables.

TinaPham
Dear Mr. and Mrs. Kool,

Thank you for taking the time to share your feedback on Tripadvisor. We were disappointed to learn about your experience and sincerely apologize for any inconvenience caused by our deposit policy.

We understand that our deposit requirement, while common for some restaurants, stems from our commitment to sustainability and a personalized dining experience. With only 11 tables and the limited ingredients, deposit allows our Chef to create each dish with the freshest ingredients possible and minimize waste. Since deposit will also be fully deducted to the bill upon dining, we hope this commitment to quality and reducing our environmental impact resonates with you.

We acknowledge that not all restaurants adopt this approach, and we completely understand your initial hesitation. We tried to reach you via email and WhatsApp to clarify the purpose of the deposit, but we apologize if these attempts were unsuccessful.

We would be truly disappointed if this single aspect of our policy deterred you from trying La Villa. We take immense pride in crafting unique culinary experiences tailored to each guest, and we're confident you'd enjoy the exquisite flavors and our warm hospitality.

We value your feedback and hope to welcome you soon to truly experience La Villa Restaurant.

Sincerely,

La Villa Team

World class gourmet cuisine !
Sep 2023 • Couples
This is an amazing dining experience. The location is a quiet street in district 2. The restaurant was previously a villa , hence the name. It is the epitome of fine dining. Exactly as you would expect, fresh white table cloths, sparkling cutlery and glasses. 
The staff are very friendly, attentive and helpful. But the reason to come here is the food. A taste of heaven in every morsel. On the evening we were there, there was a choice of 3 set menus or a la carte. We opted for one of the set menus which comprised several courses. There is an option to also add a wine pairing with each course. My wife doesn't drink so we did not try this. 
The food is simply amazing ! Beautifully presented and every mouthful is absolutely delicious. I have had the opportunity to eat in several gourmet restaurants in different parts of the world, La Villa is far and away the most delicious food I have ever eaten. 
Yes, it is a little more expensive than a typical restaurant but the entire experience of location, service, the food and meeting the chef at the end of the meal is more than worth the cost. If you are looking for the ultimate dining experience then you owe it to yourself to try this place. You will not be disappointed.

Back To The Future
Mar 2020 • Couples
This is a reminder that classic French cooking is eternal. A small menu, simple ingredients, and a chef that intuitively knows how to bring all the flavours together into delectable dishes for your palate.

Service is friendly, and personal from the Chef's wife who runs the front of house with a clear sense of pride. The timing can be a little delayed between courses, but this is a small inconvenience.

Where this restaurant lets itself down is in the decor, and therefore the vibe. Whilst we love timeless cooking, we dont need the dining room to be a throwback to 1981 as well. 

The chairs are old, the carpet is thick like your Grandma's, and while Chef Thierry will know the difference between lentils and lupins, I am quite sure he has never looked inside an interior design magazine.

So, wonderful food, with service from the heart, but prepare to be uninspired by the bright lights and old-school dated surroundings.

This came highly raved by our friends who brought us here. I was at first a bit put off when i researched this restaurant on trip advisor as the reply from the chef sounded very defensive. 

The restaurant is pretty but i must say that the food was excellent. All the courses were perfect and we didn't have any bad dish. The Foie Gras was to die for!!! It was a shame that i had to share this with my husband as he ordered another set which didn't have Foie Gras. 

The dessert was yummy but i personally find tat its a bit too heavy after stuffing ourselves. A sorbet would be a nice touch to end the excellent dinner as the weather was pretty hot.

The only disappointment was not being able to order ala carte together with the set as there were a few other dishes we would love to try (i.e. top up on Foie Gras). But we understand that the chef needs to be consistent to be able to serve us at the same time. Oh well... it just means that we have to come back again then.

I do have to agree with the chef that all concerns should be pointed out during the meal and they did address it straight away. 

The night would have been even more perfect if the air conditioning can be a bit colder. It was a bit warm when we were sitting inside. I feel like i am trying to find a pin in a haystack with this complain.

Overall, we love everything about this place and will definitely come back again on our next trip to HCMC.

La Villa – Great Food, impeccable service, a place where true hospitality is provided.
Sep 2017 • Couples
Sometimes you just cannot get enough of it – La Villa is one of those restaurants where everything comes together: Great Food prepared by Chef Thierry, served by his charming wife Tina and her team, paired with great wines from their extensive cellars. 

Our Menu degustation started with not one single but a beautiful selection of four cold amuses and a glass of their house champagne. The second, warm amuse, was served: a ravioli of duck in bouillon with a sliver of ginger! A perfect East-meets-West dish, followed by a classic vol-au-vent with veal. The more than generous slice of homemade foie gras that followed, almost made us think we were back in France. Fruit and lobster is considered by many as a no-go…but NOT at La Villa; the generous tail with orange, anis and cilantro again is a perfect example of how rules sometimes do not apply and how a great chef knows his product! 

The classic filet de bœuf with sauce aux morilles was delicious and cooked to perfection (bleu) and we would gladly come back for this dish. The cheese trolley is generous and has a great selection of predominantly French cheeses. 

To round up the meal, La Villa serves great coffee (no many good restaurants in HCMC do!) with a delicious selection of house made friandises. 
A real treat in HCMC and certainly one of my favourites in town!

Unbelievably good!
May 2017 • Family
A friend offered to take me to this restaurant. My intentions while in Vietnam were to eat nothing but Vietnamese food. This was our 13th or 14th day in Vietnam, so I agreed to eat my first Western meal in as many days. What a treat! We have dined in many fine restaurants over the years, and tend to gravitate to a tasting menu. I chose the Menu de la Villa Gourmet. My wife and two daughters had the Menu de la Villa. As we started to dine, we all realized we were in for a treat. The amuse bouche consisted four separate tiny bites: first, a shot glass of a silky beet and vegetable puree soup. Delicious! 2nd: a perfect crouton with a perfect quenelle of tapenade. 3rd, a beautiful 'fish cake' with a tiny dollop of piped aioli and some caviar. Fourth, a perfect gourgere filled with a tiny bit of bacon and gruyere. And that was just the amuse bouche! Next came another dish complements of the chef, which was a very generous quenelle of beef tartare served with a quail egg yolk and a single chip/French fry - which reminded me of french fries in Belgium. Next, we started with what we actually ordered. Higlights included the foie gras terrine, which we all agreed was the most generous portion we'd ever received in a restaurant. It was garnished with a tiny triangle of dense gingerbread, a fig poached in port, and a delicate salad of microgreens with brioche toast on the side. Delicious! The initial dish on my menu was a single lobster ravioli with a sauce that had just a hint of foie gras as well. Probably a highlight of this meal was a scallop, perfectly seared with a carrot puree, a painting of beet reduction, a spinach foam, and a garnish of tobiko. I wasn't the only one at the table who loved this dish, others had as a first course - all raved about it. The seared duck breast was cooked medium rare edge to edge, which my daughter thought must have been cooked sous vide - had a nice crust and a silky demiglace - it was excellent. The fillet had a morel mushroom sauce that no one would leave alone (that was my plate). There was a tiny glass snaplock jar of pot au feu as a side dish, and a seared piece of foie gras as well - maybe one of the best steak entrees I've had in a restauraunt, period...My wife had the seabass, also delicious, had artichokes barigoule as a garnish, delicious sauce, caviar...I only got one bite of that. The cheese service was a mind boggling array of French cheeses, I've never seen anything like it ouside of France. You will get as many servings as you like from this cheese cart, good luck choosing...Desserts were excellent. Wine pairing with the tasting menu was outstanding. The service was extremely professional. Thank you chef, for keeping your exceptionally high standards even when you are abroad. Bravo!

Just book it.
May 2017
I was asked by a local tour guide why I was going to a French restaurant when visiting Vietnam. I had no answer. I actually felt guilty because I was unsure why I was eating French when surrounded by delicious Vietnamese food...
THEN La Villa French Restaurant!
We had the wine-matched, chef's degustation (nine courses).
Magnifique.
From the amuse bouches to the cheese cart at the end, no element of this meal was left to chance. Of the courses, the beef tartate with quail egg was probably my favourite. My dining companion was "claws-down" a lobster fan. The hostess, Tina was attentive, chatty and lovely! She was happy to answer questions about the "nationality" of the food we ate and why they order food from which countries.
The wines were exquisite and to finish the meal the famous cheese cart - it seems like such a simple thing, but the cheese is flown in twice-weekly, directly from France.
I was recommended to try the roquefort bleu with local custard apple. It's a taste sensation that I will try to replicate.
Not cheap, but on par with international prices.
Thanks for a great night!

Dear Sir,

Everything is Home Made from Bread to pastries. You mentioned about salty food, you could have mentioned it while staying with us, beside French food + my cooking identity = tasty and indeed a right amount of salt in the dishes and sauces made by reduction, maybe you are not used to it.

The Smoked Salmon is wild Loch Scottish Salmon and our Striploin is Premium Black Angus Mulwarra Autralian Beef, both served generously. The average serving time for the Lunch Set, including 4 service sequencies is about 1h to 1h30, very acceptable in my opinion as we are not fast food indeed and we are actually "cooking" Sir.

ThierrySaigon
Dear Sir,

Thank you for your review and for visiting us. We remenber you and your partner and indeed you came before yesterday evening. I agree on the fact that we can't please everyone, i don't really get the "come on guys we are on 2017!", actually for me it is not really respectful, beside majority of our guests enjoyed really much the venue and find it homey, warm and welcoming... if white table clothes is old fashioned for you then many gastronomic french restaurant will be for you in that case..."authentic" or "taditional" is maybe more appropriate but still very sujective.

As your comment on the Raw Scallops Carpaccio, you mention that you don't understand what we are trying to do? Well i passed by your table to great you, you will recall that i guess, you could have asked me and i would have explained to you, but at that time you just gave me a "so far so good...". Scallop Carpaccio and Foie gras pan fried combination is one of our best seller stater, and praised by many guests since 2012, maybe it was too modern for you ;) and not enough old fashion!

We are not into fusion cuisine, i do cook what i would love to eat myself, selecting the best products and all the team is working very hard, everything is home made, from the bread to the macroons! We do focus on quality, more is less, yes but we do not cut quality just to offer more Sir, nor consistency, but consistency you can't say as you came only one time i guess... Canapes, Amuse Bouche, Mignardises are normal sequences for a restaurant of our category, but again maybe old fashion by your standards. Maybe a roof top dining with House Music would have been better for you on that night... You look as an experienced traveller by your TA profile, maybe by checking on us before hand more carefully would have helped you to choose another venue and then to avoid "mix feelings".

We do remenber that you argue with your partner on that night, it happens to all of us, and i can say by experience that it can biaised an experience as our own feelings change indeed our mood and the way to feel things...

For the Number 1 ranking on french restaurants in HCMC, well we didn't choose the ranking on TA even if we are of course vey happy with it, we are just hard working and trying our best everyday to share with our guests our passion and love of French gastronomy.

Thank you for your good comment on service, pigeon, cheese trolley, and wine selection, and hopefully you may visit us again.

Best regards, Chef Thierry

Off the charts!
Dec 2016 • Friends
I had the good fortune to host a dinner for eight friends at La Villa this weekend. It was our first trip to Ho Chi Minh so I wasn't sure what the standard of French food would be-I needn't have worried as it was truly world class.
From start to finish, it was a perfect meal. As mentioned, we were a larger group and had brought a number of bottles of wine (corkage at $25 seemed very fair considering the care that they showed in serving, changing glasses, etc.), they handled all our wines perfectly and helped to pair food to what we had. the head chef visited our table a number of times to make sure things were going well, and made the meal truly spectacular. 
All courses were delicious, but in particular, the crab ravioles in foie gras sauce, the French duck breast, and the beef fillet with pot au feu were our favorite dishes. Each one showed a high level of care and expertise combined with first rate materials.
The venue itself is a beautiful colonial style house, with a lovely garden in front were we relaxed over coffees and our final glasses of wine. The biggest surprise of all was the bill-we had expected to pay significantly more based on the meal we had. I will definitely be returning.

Brilliant dining experience
Oct 2016 • Couples
My girlfriend and absolutely loved our trip to La Villa restaurant. We both had the gourmet menu but opted to swap out the meat courses for fish - this was perfectly fine to do and every course was delightful. I really liked the scallops & the sea bass, but it's hard picking a favourite!

The food was beautifully presented (I would post some pictures but do not want to spoil it), and the tasting wines that came alongside it were perfect. Tina & all the staff were very helpful, and the chef Thierry came round and was friendly (he advised to take our time, which we were desperately trying to do to savour every mouthful)! 

I also loved the location, it took us about half an hour to get there from District 1 in HCMC & after coming through all the hustle and bustle and going down the highway we arrived on a dark tree lined road and finally some calm! It's a very good destination for a special occasion (we paid approx 270 USD for two gourmet menus and matching wines each), but you could do it a bit cheaper as a treat from the a la carte menu (especially if you spend so little throughout the trip on food as we did!)

The only tiny disappointment was that having paid the bill I nipped to the bathroom and someone had been sick everywhere and it was quite unpleasant - not the restaurant's fault but rather the clientele - but not the last memory you want!

Thanks La Villa!

ThierrySaigon
Dear Stephanie,

Thank you for visiting us, we are sorry your experience with us was "so-so", however your review is a bit lacking details. Concerning dress code we do prefer "smart casual" and this is written down on the confirmation email we sent to our guests, in a tropical country difficult to impose each customer to wear a tie and jacket...

For the inside set up , our dining room, you mention that it is bright, i thought "bright" was a good adjective, don't really know what you expect, we do set up our tables with white tableclothes and place candle light on tables, i never found that our place was too brightly lit up, for some others it could be just the opposite.

Maybe are you mistaken our restaurant with another location, kindly double check the restaurant name as it happens quite often.

Concerning the other noisy patrons, well a restaurant is a place where you accept to share space with other dinners, i agree that sometime some big tables could speak a bit too loud but it does also make a restaurant "a restaurant".

Last thing is that we don't recall any comment on site recently bringing up the issues you meet and comment here on TA, next time kindly ask to talk to our Maitre D or management in view to make you more comfortable for the time you are with us.

Thank you and best regards, Chef Thierry

Fantastic experience, excellent food
Aug 2016 • Business
Visited La Villa for dinner with some business associates to cap off our Ho Chi Minh trip.

Located away from the hustle and bustle of pretty much everything else, the little restaurant was a pleasant surprise in many ways.

The ambiance was great - quiet, simple, yet elegant. In fact, it was rather informal. Perhaps I am just used to the feel of fine dining establishments in western countries.

The staff were excellent - attentive, but not intrusive. The Owner/Manager of the establishment (Tina), was always present in the dining room providing great info on the food being served. 

As we tried the degustation menu, inevitably there would be dishes that some in our group would not try - Tina managed to persuade, and to our less adventurous dining companions' surprise, whatever they shovelled into their cautious mouths was, as it turned out, wonderful.

Together with the well thought-out wine pairing, the degustation menu was better than good. Price wise, I would say it's more than fair, considering the quality of what we were presented.

All in all, I would dare say it was one of the most satisfying (fine) dining experiences I've had.

Delightful, Decadent, Delicious
Aug 2016 • Friends
We had a remarkable, decadent, delicious, delightful dinner at La Villa French Restaurant - Ho Chi Minh City, last night. This was our second visit this year. We were celebrating our wedding anniversary with friends this time. And, I highly recommend this treasure in District 2 to all of you for a special night of dining in Saigon. My husband and I have been in Vietnam for just over a year and prior to this we visited a number of other countries in Southeast Asia. The only comparable restaurant, was Joel Robichon, in Bangkok. La Villa has is located in an charming, white colonial style home, with gardens in the courtyard. The dining room has high ceilings and although the room is large, the seating has created a comfortable, private experience for all the diners who are visiting any given evening or day. They serve both lunch and dinner. The staff anticipates your needs and is helpful, kind and attentive. The owners are accessible and friendly to whatever extent you chose them to be. We personally, enjoyed the company. You can chose from Pre-set menu's of 4 or 5 courses, or you may also select from an a la carte menu. You also have the choice of a wine pairing, which most of did. The wine selections were delightful and they complimented each course perfectly. The restaurant is generous with 'special' additions. We had a trio of amuse' bouche when we first sat for dinner; eggplant terrine, warm tomato soup and a olive tapenade on tiny toast. They followed this with another amuse', beef samosa with a yogurt sauce. This was the one thing I didn't think really fit with the meal. It seemed a little off base. I had the five course menu; crab ravioli with the decadent foie gras cream sauce...i scraped the sauce from the bowl after finishing the ravioli it was SO GOOD! This was followed by a sea scallop with foams of all flavors, Beef Tenderloin, a generous Cheese Cart that allows you to eat as much as you like and a chocolate filled pastry with fresh banana sorbet. They surprised us again, with a quadruple setting of deserts treats after this, dessert wines and a trio of digestion drinks too. I loved the wines. I am still dreaming about them. We highly recommend this amazing restaurant.

Utterly disappointed. Inflexible policies
May 2016 • Couples
We had a list of 7 restaurants we really wanted to visit and were able to fit only 4 during this trip. Now we really regret to include this as 1of the 4. 
We were told during when making our reservation that last order for lunch was 1.30pm. Very surprising but we decided to go for it even though we had our buffet breakfast at 10am, after considering the many positive reviews in Tripadvisor.
To be on the safe side, we went through the online menu and decided on our order beforehand. We also made the effort to include some buffer and give ourselves ample time to get there. Unfortunately, there was a jam and the taxi took a wrong turn, so we arrived at 1.35pm. 
We were turned away even though I made it clear that I was ready to order right away. The reason provided was that they need to close at 3pm. They refused to relent even though I said I could definitely finish the meal before 3pm. I have never experienced such inflexibility in policies. 5 minutes?
Utterly disappointed, we took the taxi right back to our hotel where every dining establishment were still happy to accept customers with open arms. 
The costs to us of this dreadful experience: VND 240, 000 wasted on cab fare, the 1 hour taxi ride under the hotel sun and the previous slot wasted on this un-deserving restaurant which we will never consider again. Our experiences in Portofino, Li Bai, Trios Gourmand during this trip were excellent. So were those from our previous trips such as Sorae, Ciao Bella and Saffron. No need for this.

Fine Dining from A to Z

From the moment we arrived at the restaurant until we left the place, we found a service which was not just immaculate but also well thought. If you are a bit used to fine dining experience you will surely find a lots of high quality details displayed by the staff (the waiters & waitresses also actually see if and when you need something, without overdoing things).

In terms of food I highly recommend the set menus available, they include not just various courses to choose from but also amuse bouches, mignardises, in some case (depending on which menu your choose) a MASSIVE cheese trolley with at least 15 different quality cheeses(not the one you find in almost every HCMC supermarkets). Taste wise, the food is in my opinion very well prepared and extremely tasteful, I simply could not fault them (even though I usually deploy a very strong sense of criticism when eating in good restaurants).

I recognize that La Villa might not be for all budgets and the place goes by some rules but the overall experience, value for money and level of service & attention in particular make this place, in my opinion, the best fine dining option in HCMC at the moment (and hopefully for a lot longer).

Delicious and consistent!
Mar 2016 • Couples
I love La Villa for their degustation. 
The first time I went was about a year ago and it was absolutely delicious, the chef comes out to the table and also his partner is coming out on a regular basis to explain the dishes. We visited again in March and it was very similar. However, the menu did not change too much...and I was blown away by the degustation the first time last year. 

This year some of the dishes were absolutely amazing (e.g. lobster, foie gras, scallop) and some were 'just' good (e.g. olive tapenade, desserts; the chocolate dessert was too much - chocolate ball with chocolate ice cream and hot chocolate sauce over it - I felt a bit nauseous afterwards, but that it was my own fault of eating it). 
The dishes were very well presented and the service was very attentive.
However, the staff might not know anything about the wines if you do have a question.

I was hoping that the degustation would have been a bit more different from the last visit (though it was great). One of my friends at the table, who is a French-food lover, was not very impressed though. 
I am very happy to visit again and see if it will be as fantastic as the first time we visited.

reviews.review_text:
Brad 🇭🇰
Hong Kong, China202128 contributions
0
Michelin calibre dining and very good French cuisine in HCMC
Dec 2015 • Couples
We recently dined at La Villa during our visit to HCMC and found this restaurant to compare quite favourably to many Michelin restaurants tried in recently years. This is a nice restaurant that serves delicious French cuisine. 

Reservations were made one week prior to our visit. Restaurant confirmed via email within a few hours of our booking request. Note: La Villa is a 15 minute taxi ride (approx. VND120,000-130,000) from most District 1 hotels. Best to print a map and directions provided by the restaurant during booking. This will assist taxi driver in finding La Villa. Upon the conclusion of your meal, the restaurant will gladly arrange a taxi for your return to your hotel. 

We liked the dining environment at La Villa. There is outdoor and indoor seating, tables are well-spaced in a central room with high ceiling. Fellow diners, at least on the evening we dined here, were sufficiently quiet in their conversation, allowing a more intimate environment to persist throughout. This was very nice compared to the busy and somewhat loud restaurants we had tried elsewhere. 

As for our meal, everything tried was very good. Meal began with a variety of breads offered and a beef tartar with half poached quail egg - amuse bouche that was delicious. 

For starters, we tried the codfish with black truffle, served with sun-dried tomato and lightly applied garlic cream. This was a very nice starter, the cod was flaky and took on the truffle oils nicely, flavours were well balanced by the sun-dried tomato. We also enjoyed the duck foie gras served with toast. This was as good as expected. 

For mains, we tried the signature La Villa - a large stuffed cockerel with foie gras and black truffle. This is a large main course serving, probably enough for two diners and it tasted great. The cockerel was very well seasoned and baked, tender, moist and oh my was the truffle and foie gras stuffing nice to eat. This is a safe choice if you're not familiar or comfortable with French cuisine and it is really good. 

Our second main was the French duck breast with sauteed potatoes and foie gras. Duck was beautifully prepared and tasted perfect when taken with the foie gras. The two complemented each other wonderfully, making many delightful moist/dry bites. This was a very nice canard main. 

We ended our meal with the Cherry Clafouti, which takes 20 minutes to prepare but is worth the wait. Citrus flavoured palate cleanser, petite four and last serving of tea were provided as we wrapped up a very good fine dining experience at La Villa in HCMC. 

In the end, we felt that that La Villa did a nice job providing an excellent meal and memorable food and dining experience in HCMC. This is a very good option for those seeking fine dining experiences during their travels to Vietnam.

Fine Quality French Dining

We heard so many local recommendations that we cycled past during the day to look at the menu. The owner-wife (Tina) met us and talked us through the options. She was hospitable and really interested in our stay in Vietnam. She didn’t pressure us for a reservation and left us to look at the menu – she is a natural host. We booked for Friday evening, our last night in Vietnam.

We had the set gourmet menu. Whilst is for 5 courses, with the little extras they provide, it turns into 8 courses. All of the food is incredibly well created, well cooked and well served. Thierry, the owner-chef, puts a lot of effort into making sure a perfect taste experience. Tina and her staff create the perfect service experience. Red wine is decanted, just as it should. 

Like so many others we were amazed by the cheese trolley. We have not even seen top restaurants in France have this any more. The staff knew each of the cheeses and can help you choose – the enthusiasm for the food runs right through the restaurant.

We loved watching another table have the black truffle menu with the beef Wellington. This was sliced at the table – a lovely thing to watch.

The food is rich with sauces, in the French style, so be prepared for an authentic French dining experience. As the French do, get more of the fresh breads and dip up all of the lovely flavours. 

We were asked many times about the food and service during the meal and Thierry met all of the tables at the end of the night. Faultless.

Lovely food, great desserts and cheese selection
Sep 2015 • Couples
This was a great meal in a beautiful setting, and if you want really good French food in HCMC this is the perfect choice. It's a bit far from the centre (south of the river) but absolutely worth going to. There are set menus for 990,000 and 1,290,00 as well as more expensive tasting menus and an extensive a la carte menu. The staff were warm and chatty as well as attentive, and the restaurant is quiet, elegant and atmospheric. It was raining when we visited but there is a sweet terrace/garden where you may be able to eat when it's fine. Even though we were eating quite late (9pm, and we were even later, as we got lost on the way) they never rushed us, and allowed us to order souffles and cheese at the end of the meal. The cheese cart is huge and you can choose as many cheeses as you want! The wine list has a good selection from about 750,000 upwards. One of the amuses was a delicious steak tartare, and my favourite dish was the scallop sashimi starter (a sort of deconstructed Coquilles St Jacques). There was also a lot of foie gras and truffle in the dishes, which were rich as well as beautifully presented.

Best meal in Vietnam
May 2015 • Couples
My wife and I live in Vietnam and we recently tried La Villa for the first time. This was definitely the finest meal I've eaten in Vietnam with all the factors covered....food was superb, service was excellent and the atmosphere/decor is A class. Tina and team were very hands on and it made for a special experience. We both had a set menu which had 5 dishes from appetizer to dessert....but what was interesting was that also provided 5 other food samplers on top of the standard meal including beef tartar, small tomato soup, etc. I am not sure if this is standard or not but it surely led to one outstanding meal and i need to cut back on food intake for the next few days. 

I can tell you that what was also incredible was the ambiance in addition to the food. we sat outside by the pool which had an excellent misting fan ... so it was cool even on a hot evening and it kept all the bugs away. we also noticed that the seating was very wide apart so it was as if we had our own private dining experience. we literally could not hear any other people although the restaurant was full that night...inside and out. A real testament to fine dining especially in Vietnam.

the meal is pricy but well worth it...and you would only go to La Villa if you want to pay for a quality meal experience. If you are after cheap, mediocre french food, this is not the place.

btw, we saw tina the next day at lunch at another restaurant and she recognized us and said hello. Nice to see her so friendly and personable in and out of the restaurant.

High class service and food.. Beware of bugs when seated outdoor
May 2015 • Couples
Tina and crew provided awesome service making sure that all the dishes are served so that guests are aware of what they are eating. No complains about the food and the chef did an extremely good job for all the dishes.

As there were 4 of us, we ordered 2 set meal and 2 ala carte as we are not allow to switch the food from the set meals.. We've ordered the terrine, pan seared foie gras, duck, steaks and scallops and all went out EXTREMELY delicious. We had the foie gras with the homemade bread from the restaurants and it's really awesome. 

We were glad that we picked the outdoor seatings as the atmosphere indoor were quite dull. We were impressed by the outdoor seatings but here are a few points I was particularly disappointed about:

Our table were right under a big tree and once in awhile bugs or leaves from the tree will fall on our plates. Though the staffs did try to clear the table and sweep the things off the table, it didn't particularly help as they have to do it pretty often. 

Though insect repellant spray was provided, it didn't really help as after the dinner, I've suffered ALOT of insect bites. We really love the outdoor seating but would strongly suggest the restaurant to provide other forms of insect repellent (probably under the table?) as a preventive measures.

Overall I would highly recommend La Villa. The good and atmosphere (outdoor) is definitely very romantic. I would have given 5 stars for the review if I had not been bitten by the insects (I wasn't expecting to be bitten by bugs when eating in a fine dining place).

Here's some recommendation for those who are looking to visit La Villa. If you want to avoid getting bitten, highly recommend the indoor seatings. If you prefer to still go with the outdoor seatings, suggest wearing a pair of jeans/pants. Otherwise bring along your own insect repellant patch!

Perfect dinner to end our vacation
Apr 2015 • Friends
Everything about this dinner went perfectly.

First, the people. Staff were attentive and professional. The serving of every dish was perfectly coordinated between two or sometimes 3 service staff for our table of three. It was also nice of the chef to come out to say hi at the end of our dinner. The waitresses were also very proactive in asking if we needed a cab while we were paying the bill.

Second, the ambience - the beautiful mansion made for a romantic setting for couples as well as a comfortable environment for groups.

Third, THE FOOD. We settled on the La Villa Gourmet set menu and were blown away by the little starters and every single dish thereafter...
- amuse bouche of steak tartare with quails egg (I felt the little French fry that came with it overpowered the delicious but delicate flavours)
- crab ravioli cooked just right with a delicious homemade foie gras sauce. Enjoyed the touch of fried onions with it.
- large seared scallop which was well balanced with vegetable purees
- the beef came perfectly medium rare with foie gras and a side of beef stock/soup. Definitely the highlight of the dinner for the two guys I was with! 
- great selection on the cheese tray from mild sorts to strong and with varieties of cow, goat and sheep cheese to pick from
- chocolate pastilla with a lovely sorbet. My first time trying this dessert and i loved it. 
- sweet endings of four little treats (the lemon macaron being my favourite) with a little cup of tea.

Definitely on par with (or even surpasses!) some of the best (and way more expensive) French restaurants I've been to in other Asian cities!

an epicurean triumph !
Apr 2015 • Couples
I had wanted to come to this restaurant for a long time but due to scheduling conflicts and the restaurant being full I've had to wait until now. I certainly had high expectations coming here given all the incredible reviews I've read on TripAdvisor. And after the incredible lunch I had the day before at Trois Gourmands which is in the same neighborhood I felt this place might let me down. But La Villa French Restaurant in District 2 of HCM City delivered on so many levels it was astonishing. First, was the ambiance of the place. It is simply a lovely and aesthetic restaurant which I felt was worthy of photos it was that nice. Next were the servants; they were lovely, educated on the dishes, and spoke excellent English. Last but certainly not least is the food !! And it was incredible. First we tried a combination of the pan seared fois gras and the goose liver terrine which was not on the menu but they made specially for us upon our request. This appetizer was breath taking and certainly rivals the fois gras at Arturs Restaurant in Bangkok. Next was crab ravioli which was so fresh and succulent. The final appetizer was the possibly the best lobster bisque I've ever tried in my life. It was a piece of artwork and a culinary masterpiece; am I running out of superlatives yet?? Our main course was the beef tenderloin and this didn't disappoint either. It was lean yet full of flavor and was accompanied by another piece of pan seared fois gras which my girl friend aggressively inhaled. We had 2 glasses of wine; a white which was just ok and a red which was delicious. Perhaps the only thing I didn't enjoy was the pre-meal mojito which I found strange in taste. We didn't have enough room for dessert but were given complementary cookies which were both aesthetic and delicious. This was one of the best dining experiences of my life and I encourage everyone to try this place at least once in your lives!

A truly unexpected, wonderful experience in Saigon.
Jan 2015 • Solo
Tonight I was craving a special dining experience in Ho Chi Minh City where food tends to be variations on one note, Vietnamese. 
I sought out an elegant French restaurant with refined food and atmosphere. I turned to Trip Advisor and selected La Villa. After a relatively longish cab ride, I landed on a quiet road in the 2nd Disrict, lined with lovely gated villas.

I was welcomed at the street, in front of a beautiful villa; very romantic setting with lovely lighting and a few tables set around a pretty pool. I chose to sit inside and it was just lovely.
The food was so wonderful as was the refined, lovely setting and service.
I was served several very special amuse bouche, each both beautiful and delicious. 
I selected a fois gras with Madeira soaked figs for my first course and seared scallops for my entree. I have not had such delectable fois gras since last in Paris. The scallops were a work of art with a plate of foamed dollops in green and carrot nada yellow purée that had tiny violas which became tiny stems. Gorgeous and yummy.

Trip Advisor rate this quaint French restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City district 2 as the best. 3 of us booked and went there to try it out. we decided that to know if they are the best we must try their best. Vietnam has great French food.

This time, I wanted to try the specialty of the house, the cockerel "La Villa" style (le coquelet en français donc).

Fabulous old school French restaurant
Apr 2014 • Couples
Set in a lovely ex-colonial mansion, this a really delightful old school French restaurant and is just perfect for special occasions.

We came here as a treat on our honeymoon and ordered the 10-course tasting menu with accompanying wines. Great value compared with what you'd pay for something similar back in the UK or Europe, so it's definitely worth a splurge if you're into fine dining. Probably best not to eat too much during the day, as even though it's a tasting menu, the portions are huge!

The tasting menu comprised of various canapes and starters, two mains, two desserts and cheese. You can choose whether you want half glasses or full glasses of wine with each course, but unless you fancy keeling over half way through, it's perhaps best to opt for the half glasses....

The food is ridiculously good - highlights for me were the homemade foie gras, the queen scallop and the baked custard apple dessert. The service throughout was incredible, very non-intrusive and polite. You can tell the owners have really set out to recreate a wonderful, typically French dining experience. While you're there, you pretty much forget about the noise, mopeds and heat right outside!

Tina, the chef's wife, does front of house and she's an absolute delight to talk to, really friendly and charming.

Definitely a must for special occasions while in Saigon.

Such creativity/boldness does meant that not every dish works for everyone - my husband and my choices worked superbly well for us, but not all the way through for my step son and his wife (the carpaccio of scallop for instance didn't do it for my daughter in law) but in my view, that is the fun of going somewhere that is so much better than anywhere else I have been to in Vietnam (or even Asia in recent years)

As well as the food being exceptional, it would be hard to find better service. So professional. So slick. So efficient in all respects. 

My only two minor comments would be (a) either improve the lighting in the garden so that one can read the menus (although that would probably spoil the romantic ambience - so perhaps torches better) and (b) have some low music in the garden so one isn't forced to listen to a fellow diner telling his life story to his date. These are not criticisms by any means as for my husband I this was an exceptional dining experience and one we would definitely wish to repeat (indeed we are considering for lunch today) 

It is of course more expensive than a lot of restaurants but at about £50 per head including wine exceptional value for the overall experience 

This shouldn't just be in the restaurant listing on TA in my view - it should be on the list of the top 10 things to do in HCMC as it is not just a meal out, rather a destination dining experience (but do make sure your driver knows where it is as it's quite a way from downtown HCMC and although we were lucky with our driver, I can imagine others will have difficulty of finding it)

Well done to everyone at La Villa for providing confidence back to me that one can eat well in HCMC

Thankfully we had a reservation,whilst a number of tables were empty when we arrived by the end of the evening all tables were taken. We were greeted by Tina who introduced herself as the owner and hostess,. such a charming lady! Tina was happy to go through the menus and explained the differences.
My partner ordered from the lobster menu, this was lobster done 3 ways. I ordered from the a la carte menu. The wine list is impressive and showcases a number of European wines, we subsequently decided on a French Riesling. 
The entrees and mains were fabulous everything served was beyond perfect. The food was absolutely delicious! We finished off with the souffle, this has to be one of the best souffles that I have ever eaten.
The staff are faultless in their professionalism. This is 5 star dining equal to some of the best restaurants in Europe or Australia and it is all delivered with a smile and everyone appears to enjoy their job.
We dined in the garden which was really beautiful with the lights dotted throughout the garden. The inside dining room is certainly reminiscent of a French drawing room with high ceilings and beautiful curtains.
If someone had said that we would have one of the most enjoyable dining experiences of our lives in Ho Chi MInh City I would not believe them. Yet that is exactly the evening we had and the service continued with the cab driver being told in Vietnamese our destination.
If we ever go back to Ho Chi Minh City La Villa will be at the top of our list.

BuckhurstHillbilly
Essex331 contributions
0
Timewarptastic but mostly very tasty.
Dec 2013 • Family
This restaurant is one of the most unusual that I have eaten in but I would not let detract from the food which was, mostly, excellent.
I guess because La Villa is housed in a remarkable old colonial Indochine house I arrived with certain expectations. It was also raining hard so we were unable to appreciate the full outdoor/indoor ambiance of the place.

One is greeted upon arrival in one's taxi, (it's a bit off the beaten track), by Madame the local hostess or one of her besuited minions. Led through the garden into what must have once been the epitome of late 19th century elegance. I would imagine the building was renovated during the 1980s and it wasn't a sympathetic refurb. Heavy red velvet drapes, a cuckoo clock etc. Such a pity.

There is no shortage of male and female staff catering to your needs and explaining the menu and concept. Prices are high for Vietnam but fair for the UK for this type of experience.
We decided to stick to the a la carte menu as my son and I fancied the raw scallop followed by the steak and foie gras. These were perfectly prepared/well cooked though my husband's choices were poor and he didn't enjoy his meal.
Amuses bouches came first which included a toffee'd cherry tomato,(truly!), a mini blini with smoked salmon and soft cheese, and something else which was quite vile.
A pre appetiser of mini tuna tartare followed stopped by a raw quail egg was then served which was quite amazing!
La Villa has a charming, attractive and highly knowledgeable female sommelier who will assist with your choice of wine from a very extensive, mainly European and fairly priced wine list.
Following the hors d.oeuvres and main courses we decided it wasn't really our style of restaurant, we really found it a strange place, so we ordered coffees and a taxi to return us to our hotel. I must stress this is purely a personal opinion as the mainly eastern clientele seemed to live it and the staff and hostess are extremely hospitable. There was even a couple with well behaved tiny one in a high class dining on the night we were there.

The espressos came with some home made orangecello, and 3 home made petits fours including yummy, tiny lemon macaroons.

We probably would rate La Villa with 7.5 out of 10 for food but ambiance wise, it really didn't do it for us I'm afraid.

Disappointed with the service!!!
Dec 2013 • Friends
We went here as a group of three couples. For fine dining this place needs to change a few things. I had high expectations after reading the reviews but were thoroughly disappointed. 

Good:
Food ranged from okay to great. My fiancee and I had the tasting menu. The lamb dish was great. The sea bass was excellent. The scallops was just okay. There was nothing special about the food to make me come back. The chef and his wife came to say hi which was a nice touch. But honestly I am not sure why it got a number one status on tripadvisor. 

Bad:
Holy moly. How did they not train their staff better than this?! During our 3 plus hours dinner (took forever for each course to arrive) there were so many times we had absolutely no service. They left our wine and water bottles on a table close by. They never refilled our glasses. We had to get up at least five times to pour our own drinks. When the waiters saw this instead of rushing over to pour it for us and apologize they just let us finish. I dont drink alcohol so the entire night I had to keep on asking for water to be filled. The waiters didnt seem busy. They just seem lost. 

Fine dining takes a few hours but 3.5 hours is ridiculous. They cant manage time very well. The cheese course was smelly as expected but after trying it and not liking it. I had to put paper over it to cover the smell because no one came to remove the plate for half an hour. 

There were quite a number of instances with bad service. I would not recommend this place to anyone. Nothing special about the food and crappy service. Of the numerous restaurants we visited during our trip, this was the worst.

Written December 22, 2013
ThierrySaigon
Dear Mr/Ms Potatorice,

My name Tina, i am wife of Thierry and i would like to response your review as i am personally who took care of your table on that day. Firstly thank you for your positive comments on food especially for the lamb. However our tasting menu is not the menu you have mentioned. Degustation menu would be 10 courses per person and do not have lamb and sea bass.
I remembered upon your table's arrival, your fiancee had asked me to seperate the bill in 3 different bills for 3 couples and we did refused as our billing system is per table. 
I took the orders for your table and there were a la carte ( 2 persons), 1 Menu Petite Villa 3 courses, 1 menu de La Villa 4 courses and 1 Menu Villa Gourmet 5 courses. Usually the menu 3-4 courses might take only 1.5-2 hours to finish and 5 courses menu is about 2.5 hours. There would have one -two courses that you or other people had to wait as the number of dishes per person were not the same and the longest menu you had was 5 courses. However the duration of meal is still depended on how long you have eaten for each course. And i forgot to mention that all the above menus are excluded 2 compliment courses from the restaurant. Foe Fine dining we do not think 3.5 hours is too much and your table have arrived at 20:00 and finish 23:30, we think it is possible.
As a person who took care of your table since service started, i had come to your table each course to ask if everything was alright and i think if it was not as good as your expectation, you should mention to me as we would appreciate to correct it and improve immediately.
So far most of our guests did enjoyed La Villa food and service was always at attention and not was bad as you mentioned. Maybe there was one time the water did not fill up and i did ask our staff to notice. Sorry for this mistake as it was at weekend and we got a miss service of pouring water at your table. We will take a good look at this issue.
For the cheese, we did have our cheese trolley which have more than 20 kinds of different french cheese and we did not think you could not find any of your favorite? and again if you did choose some cheese which you do not like then you can return to us. We believe French Cheese is not that bad and you might order some strong cheese which are smelly and could be sheep or goat cheese. But again it is impossible to leave your cheese plate half an hour without any notice of staff as they might think you did not finish. You know it is not nice if we came to clear your cheese plate just after ordering as we should give you sometime to enjoy it! but you could ask the waitress to clear if you taste it at beginning and did not like it.
When my husband/ Chef of La Villa came to ask you about the meal and service and you did not mention anything instead of "everything was good" so we assume that you got a not very bad dinner.....

Thank you for your comments again
Kind Regards
Tina

Excellent. Come hungry!
Nov 2013 • Friends
I am very glad we persevered with this resteraunt as the previous night our hotel concierge had told us that it had closed down a month ago!

 Much has been written about the setting, food and service. All excellent and deservedly so.

Do not come here expecting small portions of nouvelle cuisine. The helpings are hearty, and before you get to your starter there is the bread basket, a trio of amuse bouche(the caramel tomato being especially noteworthy), and a mini steak tartare to get through.

I had a very classical French meal of caillette followed by andouillette with risotto, and my wife had the crab ravioli and the veal with a wheat risotto with foi gras.

We were way too full for pudding, and just had a coffee with complimentary petit fours and a shot of iced orangecello.

US$139 inc wine which is a bargain for food of this quality. We will be back over Christmas.

Good place for a speacial occasion
Nov 2013 • Family
I had been to La Villa for two times. The first time when I was moving here, I was impressed with the food and service. So this time my family visited me, I took them here. The restaurant is in district 2. I would recommend you to book before you go there. It's an old French house. The set up is quite formal. But you don’t need to dress up. No dress code at all :-) The menu can be Alacart or Set Menu. The first time I chose set menu. It was very nice but it's too much for me. So this time, we ordered only starter and main course. But we got a lot more than we ordered anyway:-) Started with good bread, followed with the complimentary from the house, and then something before starter, so even before starter I feel quite full already. We loved all the dishes. We ordered beef, duck and chicken. All were good. At the end we were too full, but we could not say no to the sweets, so we ordered one chocolate cake to share. The price here is consider expensive when compare with other restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City. But if you compare the same type of Food, quality and Set Up in other countries, this is a very reasonable price. But anyway, it's not the place that you go for a dinner every day. It's a special place for a special occasion.

Nice & cozy place! <3
Aug 2013
I love the atmosphere here, very nice and cozy, suitable for a date or family dine-out.
We were severed with apéritif (complémentaire): canapés, breads and foie de poulet (chicken liver). The chicken liver was kinda too much and greasy, we couldn’t finish half of it. But the sugar-coated baby tomatoes were very cute and delicious, the mixture of sweetness and sour, as the starter, help “stimulate” your stomach for later dishes.
 
Le premier plat:
1. We enjoyed the Ravioles Fondantes de Crabe a lot. It was the best order of the night, very creamy, cheesy with foie gras sauce. 
2. Terrine de Foie Gras de Canard du Gers “Mi-cuite” was okey, would give it 7/10.
3. Langoustine Poèlées (scampi) wouldn’t recommend as the scampi was frozen ones, hence, they were not really fresh. But for those (esp. Vietnamese like me) who has never tried scampi, shoot ahead, it was kinda fun looking at the “prawn” with crab’s legs. Would prefer prawn or lobster, would be a lot fresher!
For main courses, we had: Sea bass, Beef tenderloin, Veal tenderloin and the Sea scallops. I love scallops and it was second best order of the night, but again, the scallops are imported, hence, it’s not as fresh as it could be, but still, very enjoyable! My parents and my spouse finished all of their dishes, so I guess they enjoyed the food here, too.
I ordered Dark choco mousse cake but we were too full to finish up. Tina, one of the owners, gave us a Rum raisin ice cream as she missed order with the orange soba. :)

Best restaurant in Saigon. A little expensive for Vietnam but woth it.
Mar 2013 • Couples
This restaurant offers French cuisine (the owner is a French chef who married a Vietnamese lady).
I would suggest to try the Tasting menus. The foie gras is really good and the duck as well.
Of course it is a bit expensive for Vietnam, but it is worth it and for that price you would never eat the same quality in Europe.
We got a "Menu Petite Villa" and we spent less then 40 euros each: we had a delicious foie gras as entrée, roasted duck breast as main and a desert. We shared 3 beers in 2. I also got an extra entrè as I wanted to taste the "Aubergine & Mozzarella Millefeulle" (not outstanding). We were offered an amuse bouche before our entrèes and also some small pastries and tea after our desert.
I went there for my birthday with my girlfriend and we really spent a nice evening and would surely go again.

IMPORTANT: the location of La Villa is not so central and you will need to take a taxi to get there so make sure you have the full address of the restaurant (and its telephone number just in case!) as well as the address of your hotel to be sure you can get home again :-)

A hidden treasure... french treat in hcmc!
Apr 2013 • Couples
A cook from south of France, a restaurant set in a serene French-styled mini-villa, a unique collection of French wines and authentic French cuisine… All this in the outskirts of Saigon, a.k.a. Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam… Sounds unreal? Well its true. A historic French colony of the 19th Century… French influence is very visible throughout the Vietnam belt… and La Villa reminds you of that French presence.La Villa – Outdoor SittingLa Villa, a cozy French restaurant was launched on Valentine’s Day 2011, is HCMC’s most popular European restaurants, and a must try! Google for top 10 restaurant’s in HCMC and La Villa will feature in the list for sure. And that’s exactly how we stumbled upon this little gourmet treat. 

We tried the vol au vent with prawns, crab on mashed peas and lemon tart...

Few suggestions... the chef Thierry is very friendly and knows what he is doing... tell him your preferences and allow him to choose a 3 course meal for you... further these guys know their wime too... so take suggestions from them as per your budget. 

Finally, get a table booked, especially if its a weekend.. the place is often fully booked. Opt for pool side if it isnt too hot... its a treat!

The Perfect Bite!
Jul 2013 • Couples
My partner and I had decided to spend our last night out at La Villa French as we had read so many wonderful reviews about the restaurant. We booked with Tina and upon arrival we were greeted by name as the staff open our taxi door and welcomed us into the restaurant. We started the the evening with an aperitif and offered a creative assortment of bite size canapés. After the canapés, they came with a delightful creamy vegetable soup. My partner and I decided to order different courses, so that way we got to try more variety. We had the Duck Foie Gras Terrine with Strawberry Chutney (absolutely amazing) and the Cailettle Provencale of Pig with Warm Goat Cheese. For our mains we had the French Duck Breast Panfried and the Pan Fried Sea Scallops with Saffron which were both served in the perfect size, not with too much cluttering the plate but very beautiful presentation. We had our dessert served out by with pool where we shared the Tropézienne Provençale (French Brioche and Kirsch Flavored Cream). My partner is also a French chef and works in Copenhagen at a Vietnamese restaurant, so he and Chef Thierry Mounon got a chance to talk a bit about the culinary arts. We ended the night with some lovely complementary bite size desserts, such as the homemade macaroons and chocolate glazed orange peel and two glasses of champagne.

Amazing Food and Wonderful Atmosphere

I was recommended to bring my girlfriend to eat at La Villa French by a receptionist at my hotel who had previously been here. First class
May 2013 • Couples
Went here for our final dinner in Vietnam, and it was indeed a worthy finish to a great vacation.

I had a liver meatball for a starter which was a pure delight. It was filled with goat cheese and served with a very discrete tomato sause, just an excellent combination.

The scallops for my second course were beautiful. They were served with a risotto that in my opinion could've been seasoned slightly more and was on the hard side, but in total a nice dish also.

The lamb tenderloin was served with a snail ratatouille that I didn't really get personally, I would have preferred a few whole ones provencale on the side, but the meat was handled well.

The cheese trolley was another highlight, a very good selection was on display. The presentation was done very quick though and the different kinds were only identified by name. Perhaps print out a card where each cheese is presented with name and characteristics, and give this to the guest in advance.

Our desserts (lemon tart and chocolate cake) were on the chilly side though, and had probably seen a fridge too close to being served.

The negative points are pretty minor though, and all in all we left very satisfied and felt we had gotten great value for money. A very pleasant experience.

An authentic Southern French Cuisine in Saigon.
Jun 2012 • Couples
La Villa is an excellent restaurant that I would recommend for anybody who want to eat an authentic and upper quality almost gastro French Food in Saigon. 

The good thing is this restaurant serves an authentic cuisine from the South of France. A cuisine made with thyme, rosemary, olive oil, garlic, aioli, tepenade, anis, pitchoulines...etc and creme de la creme for the South of France Food Conoisseurs: we can even get a home made brandade! 

Well, the dishes are perfectly cooked and they are litterally making you traveling to the South of France. I recommend:
The "Vol au Vent" with Giant Prawns and Foie Gras, Espelette and Cayenne Perfumes...
The Lamb Tenderloin with Thyme and Rosemary Stuffed Tomato with a Snails Ratatouille...
The Monkfish in the Style of “Sète” Small Vegetables and Creamy “Aioli”
La Tropézienne Provençale 

The service is good, the staff is always there when you need it without sticking to you and putting pressure. The place is clean, indoor, outdoor, toilets... The water and the drinks are served at the right temperature. The table is regularly cleaned between each meal....

The place look nice and it's quite, especially outdoor in the garden with the swimming pool at night. I recommend this place for a date or a business dinner. Congratulation because the chef obsiously love and know perfectly the Southern Food, far, far, far away from the greasy cuisine cooked with butter... it is also a real culinary trip to the South of France.

We have visited La Villa with several good recommendations from friends and we were not disappointed at all. The food is excellent, the dishes are delicious, well prepared and technically perfect. 

This less than 2 years restaurant has a bright future if they continue with its perfectionist mentalithy. Behind this piece of southern France you can find Thierry Mounon. He is a french, experienced chef and owner. An "hotelier" as he defines himself, seems to got the "know how" to quickly stepping up his place.

Mainly based on local ingredients, some hight quality imported products, make te difference. The cheese selection is outstanding. Wine cellar could improve but still offer several good options. The place in confortable. The terrace pool side is a good option for dinner time.

The staff is really nice and kind. Just keep training them, to be closer to the professional level of the kitchen performance. Because it is Vietnam and not France, price also need to be balanced. However, it is still a good value for an special night. 

One of the best options in Saigon to have an unforgettable "haute cuisine" experience.

I dont like the decoration but I couldn't have any complaints about the food and the staff
Feb 2013 • Couples
I am Vietnamese, but I am fond of western food due to my chance to meet up with a Italian chef in HCM city, he had made so many great meals for me, but after he's gone I couldn't find any other places in HCM to give me that good food. And because I started with Italian food, So I didnt think that I would love French food, I am not sure about anyone else but to me, They are totally different from each other, one more thing, I have no knowledge about food or food culture, I just enjoy it. 
So when my Bf took me to La Villa the very first time, I didn't like it in the beginning, the Restaurant is really far from my house, and has a quite boring look...etc..., BUT when the lady boss came, things changed, she was friendly, and patient to take the order, and because her husband, the boss is the chef so we trusted her , any things she did offer us are just simply good.
 
if it for 2 persons, I think we should try french cheese trolley with a a glass of wine...

I love meat so it's all about meat to me, the Beef is fair, 7 points (but in HCM I didnt there are other places have really good steak or else, Gosh I tried all the steak houses in HCM, that one of the way to waste money); Lamb is just ok here, nothing special, I prefer something with stronger smell and more juices; well Duck breast, oh I like it, the meat is soft and the skin is lightly crunchy, and the taste is good too; ah but the Veal, if you like the soft tenderloin beef(but not so dry as tenderloin beef) and a bit different taste, you must try Veal, highly recommend it; and one of the very special dish in La Villa is Coquelet Farci "La Villa", I am not sure if I remember the name right but it is a small chicken with many things inside, a bit like spring chicken that the Italian chef made for me once, but the taste is different, and this is good too, I think that 2 persons should share the chicken (though it's small, I can finish it myself but it's ok to share than you can try other things hahaha).... 
the deserts, well, I have to say that they are just ok again(after 3 times there, we tried most of the deserts) except the 2 here, souffle(even the taste is a bit light to me, and I dont like the smell of Orange liquor but the cake is soft and melted in my mouth right away) and macaron(tomato one) but the Macaron is not in the menu, it was a gift from the lady boss, But I am sure that they usually make it, it was really good, you can ask for it I think

and the wine is ok, sorry but I love the way the Italian wine tastes so French wine just always ok to me, all I can say they have the wine reasonable price (in HCM I mean)

A superb restaurant with delightful staff.
Apr 2013 • Couples
My Partner and I had 3 nights in Saigon as part of a 2 week Vietnamese holiday. So where should we eat during our stay? We consulted Trip Adviser and opted for the No 1 rated restaurant out of 700+ to choose from.

La Villa is No 1 for a reason. In fact, lots of reasons. Even before we arrived, our reservation was dealt with swiftly and courteously by email and our last minute change of date was accommodated with charm.

The venue is delightful. Located a little off the beaten track in District 2, one travels down a narrow lane to find an attractively lit colonial style villa. But what could pass for a grand house is indeed a grand restaurant.

There is a choice of tables inside and out. We chose outside, located next to the swimming pool on a balmy April evening.

The staff were attentive throughout and the service could not be faulted. And the food matched up to both the service and ambience. Both of our starters, crab ravioli and scallop carpaccio, were delicious, with a riot of flavours.

So, if you find yourself needing dinner in Saigon, make a booking at Thierry and Tina's La Villa in District 2. You will have a lovely evening.

Very special
Apr 2013
Very special place down a side street 6 km out of the main tourist areas - 110,000VND in a cab and about 20 mins. 

Lots of lovely extras that really made the experience - gazpacho between first and main course. Some lovely breads. The crab ravioli was tasty. The mozzarella and tomato starter was a work of art. Mains were more variable. Veal was superb. Duck was a little tough but still fantastic presentation. The monkfish was very sparse and not to my palate. All in for 3 of us was $177. I've eaten in London for similar quality and price, but the location was great. A one off for us on the last night of an Asia tour. 

A few minor downsides. We too saw a couple of rats like other reviewers commented- but noting location, not totally unexpected. I also agree with other reviewers about shipping in French water. If someone wants to order it then fine, but please give us some options. Carlsberg works out at around $7 for half litre which is probably unwarranted. Also please ask the waitress not to clear away the plates until everyone stops eating- it makes the slowest feel they are being pressured. 

All in, a great night with only minor gripes. But very pricey for HCM.

Almost Perfect But ..
Mar 2013 • Couples
There is no doubt that La Villa is a gem in Saigon. Really serious French food, an eclectic French wine list and value for money. The traipse out by Saigon standards felt like I was heading into Cambodia but after a 20 minute tour down highways and byways we made it. Be prepared for that worrying few moments when you wonder if the driver knows the destination. Civilization suddenly hits in the form of a compound complete with international schools, big five accounting firms and brand name foreign company headquarters, so you sense you are getting close. The restaurant is over the road and down a lane. We were told by the proprietress that this was where a lot of foreigners lived, which was the first moment one wondered about the quality. Nothing worse than a "white-man enclave" to lower standards in Asia. But the restaurant seems to have survived the worst of that. The Prix fixe and a la carte menus are very interesting and you would need to be clueless not to find your ideal menu. The staff are interesting, clearly well trained and apart from some translation issues genuinely a pleasure. So what knocks the one star off? Basically the desserts! Now lets put all this in perspective. Any restaurant that runs a "cheese chariot" in Asia is brave indeed and needs to be supported. Imagine the potential waste as your un-brave locals and expats confront Roquefort and Epoisses. The chef clearly has this waste problem in mind when he opts for pre-cooked tart bases and cookies in the desserts. Can we blame him, should we feel cheated, especially at these prices? Well in my view yes we should. The reason is this guy knows his stuff and knows the point I am making. This is probably the best French restaurant in the country, so why settle for less than the best. Of course I would and will go back. The night we were there the lady of the house spent far too much time chatting away with one set of regular clients. A no-no in a fine restaurant. Am I being picky? But of course!!

I was expecting 'amazing' and I just got 'good'.
Feb 2013 • Couples
I went here after reading all the great comments posted on Tripadviser.
It was good.. but not amazing as I was hoping for.
The whole time I compared the food quality to that of Trois Gourmands, and I have to say, it just didn't measured up.
The restaurant looks amazing. And I would give this place full marks for the atmosphere. But there were a few things that let the whole experience down for me.
First, I asked the waitress what kind of wine is the house white wine. They didn't know and had to go and get the bottle to show me. You think they would know what the house wine is.
I had the set menu. It was all very nice. The food was presented like how I would expect a fine dinning restaurant to be. My duck breast was cooked perfectly.
The only let down of my meal was the desert. The apple tart. Served luke warm. I'm sure it was meant to be served hot.
The only bad thing about the meal really was at the end they had a few extra sweets to finish. A mini cake which was just dried. (Less is more. They shouldn't have served that at all) A macaroon and a piece of dark chocolate that was way too hard because it just came out of the fridge.

All in all, I think they did a good job.
If my expectation wasn't so high, I think I would have liked it more. But being the number 1 rated restaurant in HCM, and having been to another french restaurant Trois Gourmands not too long before this, all I can do is compare the two, and with this I was a little disappointed and felt like I wasted a dinner with food that was just good, considering I don't have many dinner on this short trip and being in a city with so much amazing food.

thatswhatjennisaid

Worthy of its #1 Ranking - Don't Miss this Place!
Jan 2013 • Couples
I have dined at Le Cirque, The French Laundry, Per Se, Le Cinq, Citronelle, and many other top restaurants around the world and I feel I know great food when it is before me. La Villa certainly offers wonderful cuisine, with quality ingredients well sourced (foie gras showed up in multiple courses; truffles were plentiful; the cheese cart offers a wide selection of cheeses imported from France). Not only does La Villa offer fine food, it does so at an incredible value for those of us coming from Western locales (approx $50 USD pp for a 5 course meal incl foie gras and truffles!).

As other reviewers have mentioned, the restaurant is housed in a stately French Mansion across the river from central Saigon, with a team of Vietnamese local staff at the ready to take care of your every need. At the head of operations is a friendly and gracious petite Vietnamese lady and her French husband who serves as the executive chef. The setting is romantic and lovely both indoors and out. Dining indoors you'll have the benefit of air conditioning and dining outdoors you'll have the delight of the evening ambiance and soft lighting of the pool. And for the previous reviewer who commented negatively on the "wildlife" outdoors- those scurrying creatures are simply geckos and they keep to themselves on the garden walls and present no complications nor introduce any sanitation problems to the facilities. 

Perhaps the one suggestion I have for the staff at La Villa is to more carefully manage the timing of the food presentation. While most of our course flowed in a well timed manner, there was a bit of a gap between the first and second course that was not explained by our wait staff nor the owner (who was making the rounds). Hopefully it was just a one time delay due to a full house of patrons, but every successful restaurant needs to keep a watch on these sorts of things and be ready to explain to customers (or distract them with an intermezzo) when delays crop up unavoidably. 

On to the food itself...husband and I both chose the 5 course menu and the star studded stand outs from our selections were the foie gras terrine (so delicious!), the crab ravioli, and the sea bass. Don't miss this items! And the amuse bouche items were a lovely surprise - I am going to borrow the idea for the caramel dipped baby tomatoes for my next dinner party- what a delightful little way to get things started. 

We will certainly visit La Villa again should we return to Saigon and we highly recommend the restaurant to everyone.

Exclusive French Dining
Dec 2012 • Couples
This restaurant deserves its accolade as the best in Ho Chi Minh city. It is located in what I would call the French expatriate area, so it's worth a pre-dinner stroll to admire the beautiful French colonial architecture in the area. The manager/owner is Vietnamese Tina Trang Pham and her French husband who is the chef. We ate on New Year's Eve and paid $95 per person for a seven course feast, an absolute wonder of French cuisine, cooked with verve and imagination. Highlights for me were the foie-gras and black truffle ravioles, the stunning lobster tail and the sublime veal cooked to medium rare perfection. The staff are well-trained, attentive and keen to do well. Tina visited our table on a couple of occasions to check that all was in order. I believe that the cuisine served here easily ranks among the top French restaurants in London and Paris, and I'd include Le Gavroche in that. The ambience was beautifully complemented by live classical music. A small aside - I had some travel difficulty that put my visit into jeopardy. Tine gave me fantastic and effective advice on what to do and how to do it, and went well beyond what even a good restaurateur would do in terms of customer service. In fact, this is what makes La Villa so good - you are not a customer, you are a friend from the moment you step inside.

reviews.review_text:
AllisonjaneBrisbane
Brisbane, Australia346 contributions
0
Fantastic
Dec 2012 • Couples
We had the MENU DE LA VILLA which was 920,000 VND a head.
Firstly let me say you have never eaten bread rolls until you have been here. Major happy dance. I am not hung up on bread and frequently when I buy bread the chickens end up eating it but oh good golly … it was like cake - oh dear lord I could cry just thinking about the bread roll now.
At the first course stage I knew this meal was going to be on my top five of all-time best meals.
The atmosphere was lovely. You felt like you were being spoilt in a lovely surrounding. 
The Duck Foie Gras Terrine was wonderful. I had the Pan Fried Sea Scallops with Saffron and vegetables Creamy Risotto and some Chanterelles, Marine Essence and my husband had the Roasted Australian Lamb Tenderloin with Thyme and Rosemary Stuffed Tomato with a Snails Ratatouille. We swapped plates ½ way through and were impressed with both dishes. 
The Cheese Trolley was surprisingly full of options but although I really liked the young waiter - telling your customers you don’t like cheese is not a good look and when asked what a cheese was I expected the name .. not its goats cheese. Perhaps given the language differences and sometimes accents some name cards for the dessert would not go astray?
 My dessert was amazing a Millefeuille of total happiness. 
Little extras came out during the meal that just made you even more impressed. 
Our wine was lovely and I don’t recollect it being overly expensive although it was not Australian bottle shop prices.
The restaurant is in a poky little street and not all taxi drivers know where to go to get there. So get the hotel front desk to print off a map if you are not a local.
There is a great big bloody swimming pool in the front yard which must be tempting for the odd customer to dive into especially after some champers. 
Staff were lovely and the chef came out of the kitchen at the end of the night and spoke to all the guests which was a really nice touch. It was clear that there were a number of regulars there by the conversations and greetings. Always a good sign. The chef when he was talking to us noticed a little platter of chocolates and sweet things come out and took it back to be re plated as it clearly did not meet his standards. This was amazing and complimentary.
The chef helped us out when we left telling the taxi driver our hotel as our Australian accents must have confused the taxi driver given the blank look we got as we were getting in the taxi.
Sure by Vietnam standards the prices are high. But oh my gosh so worth it. You do need to make a reservation.
One of the reasons I would love to go back to Ho Chi Minh is for this restaurant.

KBWU
108 contributions
