Reasonable restaurant generally but average for Foodies looking for excellent food
Nov 2012
Restaurant is 10-15 min ride
from district 1, cost about 140-160VND. We selected the 5 course dinner which is 1,220 VM, including appetizer, fish,meat, dessert and cheese trolley.  Wine was reasonably priced , largely 800-120,000 VND. Appetizers :300-450,000 VND, Main courses :400-600,000 VND. Desserts :170-250,000 VND. So basically for set, they throw in  dessert and cheese trolley for free. Bread basket is average. Rolls although warm and soft inside has crumbling crust like biscuit.  Would prefer a normal baguette with a little chewy texture inside.
Amuse  bouche-  pumpkin soup is velvety and creamy. Good start ! For appetisers, my husband ordered truffle oil Infused  scallop carpacio. Nice combination with the refreshing salad. I ordered  Au vent with foe gras, basically is a little shrimp puff with seafood bisque sauce. Puff is hard, sprout and thyme salad is delicate and refreshing.  But didn't know where the foe gras went into...

For  the fish course, i had the Cod dish with calamari as main course. They should have written clearly that the cod fish is preserved cod fish not fresh cod fish. Menu described dish as  "Pan fried COD fish **slighted salted *" with olive oil".  It should have been written as "Pan fried Salted COD fish" . But overall the dish tastes quite good , the warm calamari with chopped olive in balsamic dressing is nice, except salted cod fish has a slight bitter taste . My Husband had Crab meat on bed of mashed pea for his fish course . Ok but not excellent. His meat selection - tenderloin has great texture but mashed potato with truffle oil and herb too complex. .  My meat course- the veal is welldone when I ask for medium.   The accompanying sauteed porcini  is however excellent, one of the best ever... 
Cheese trolley spread is good. Our choice of Camembert and blue cheese did not disappoint. However , as a dessert fanatic, I I was little disappointed with the dark Chocolate mousse .Probably due to the quality of chocolate used. Petite fours' macaroons  are surprisingly ok... The hot thyme
tea serve in espresso cup  is a unique ending to the meal.
 
In conclusion, price for the 5 course set is reasonable for its quality, portion . Generally, a reasonable restaurant.. But for Foodies, maybe just an average restaurant.. We may return if we reside in HCM but may not return if we are tourists. As of now , I  am still a  tourist . Spent  3,550,000 VND or usd 177 for 5 course dinner for two with a bottle of wine and a bottle of water .  Wanted to rate  it 3.5 star only  but as there is no half star, I would rate it 4 star for its extraordinary service rendered !

Number 1 for good reason - don't hasitate go here
Nov 2012 • Business
Overall a wonderful evening at La Ville.
The owners are proud of their resturant and should be. They are created a great mix of great food, great wine, solidly service, amazing cheese in a lovely setting which just so happen to be there home too !!
We booked on the day "just invade we needed to" and we did need to as by 8pm all tables were gone on a Thursday night.
We were meet at the taxi and welcomed to the resturant. The offer of pre dinner outdoor drinks was tempting but on a hot sticky night we headed for the a/c.
The menu is cleverly thought out and combinations to suit you tasty and purse are there. Naturally we got totally excited and went for the 5 course gourmet (basically you chose a starter, fish course, main course and desert - in between all of that Rees cheese too).
All the food we had was carefully balanced and seasoned to the right level. This is a skilled chef so sit back and try things you would normally try. Would love to have done to Degistation but at 10 courses it scared us :-)
Basics are "save up and come here". Yes it's a bit pricey compared to a street stall in Ho but this is a world class resturant - so for that the price is about right.
The owners come over to the tables often which is a wonderful touch.
Lots of little hidden dishes come out - a platter of "amuse bouche", a mushroom soup, a liquor, a macaroon, a thyme tea.
These touches are nice surprises that just add to a great evening.
The service is good - maybe not quite 5 star but I don't like 5 star service so it was perfect for me.
The ambiance was buzzing in a full resturant so we actually took desert outside by the ppool just to get a bit of quiet time.

Worth the hype!!!
Oct 2012 • Friends
After living in Saigon for a few years, I finally made the trek to Thao Dien to try La Villa. It was worth the trip...and then some. There's a lot of good food to be had in Saigon...but there's very little great food. La Villa provided the best overall dining experience I've had...so I'd say it deserves to be the number 1 restaurant on this website.

We decided to order off the a la carte menu so that we could order more appetizers. The scallop carpaccio was delightful - the texture contrast between the scallop and the shaved parmesan and the jicama salad that was served atop the carpaccio was fantastic. We also had the calamari ravioli, which was one of the tastiest things I've eaten anywhere. Then we had the mullet and crab brandade, which was served with sundried tomato slices and basil a la classic caprese salad - great presentation. For mains we tried the codfish and the veal - both mains were cooked to perfection. I could eat an entire plate of either the seared tomatoes that came with the fish or the porcini mushrooms that came with the veal. In fact, said porcini mushrooms might have been the tastiest thing I had all night. We finished our meal with selections from the cheese tray, which is appropriately bountiful. 

The restaurant itself is beautiful. I would call it understated elegance...a welcome relief in the architectural quagmire that is SE Asia. It would, however, benefit from a nicer bathroom...

I would unequivocally recommend La Villa for anyone celebrating a special occasion, seeking something delicious or simply needing to escape the organized chaos that dominates most of Saigon. 

One final note: given the quality of the overall experience, the prices are more than reasonable. I can't see how any experienced diner could possibly scoff at La Villa's pricing!

Very good experience
Oct 2012
We had set dinner, 700k for 3 courses, very reasonable. Before serving the starter, there were 3 mini appetizers. One of which is a sugar coated cherry tomato which is very cute and the tomato very tasty, and you can tell right away they use quality raw materials. We had duck liver and veggie soup for starters, the duck foie GRAS was not so oily as goose foie gras, and we really liked it. The veggie soup was tasty, it came with a big head shrimp, which is not the tasty kind but the seasoning gave it a nice aroma.
For mains, i had Australian beef, which was cooked just right, and the mashed potato was sprinkled with black truffle, also nice. My husband had seabass fillet with pasta, which was a bit disappointing because the fish was not the fatty kind as we had expected and thus a bit dry, while the pasta was overcooked, maybe that's how the French make their pasta, but we much prefer the Italian style which is hard in the center. 
For dessert, the apple tart was good while chocolate cake was way too sweet, felt like eating sugar powder mixed with chocolate mousse. 
Finally there was some free dessert and alcohol drink.
Service was very good, a girl greets you at the door, the owner/chef came out once and his wife was there most of the night and checking in on how everything went at the right moment. 
Overall very good, food was tasty although did not blow me away, but the service made up for it. Would go back if we visit hcm again.

La Villa French Restaurant
Mar 2012 • Friends
Having lived here for 2yrs, I found this to be the most expensive restaurant In VN. I would only recommend it for a special occasion, want to impress some one or self indulge with money being no object. I attended with 2 ladies who dressed formally for the occasion (which set the alarm bells ringing) on a Wednesday night, a young VN couple were at one table and a group of 6 VN at another. Staff out numbered patronage 3 to 1; this distracted from the atmosphere. The Villa was built early 1900s and is best described as elegant as were the staff, who were well trained and very professional, I felt I should have worn a tuxedo and slicked my hair down to fit in with the decor. No one would be so crass as to drag out there camera here and take pictures. We all sucked air thru our teeth when we viewed the prices. Main course $50 to $100+, wine similarly priced (if the menu was expressed in VND you would be looking at millions and a foreigner would probably require an ambulance outside). In VN you seldom cook as eating out is so cheap and $15 for a main course would be considered very expensive. (by comparison, there are many menu variety buffets, all under $50 with wine, offered thru out HCM and are spectacular). The food was very well presented, tasty, highlighted with delicate sauces and trimmings. A French model would feel at home. There are not many French Restaurants in HCM or VN all have a similar quality of food and taste but at a much, much cheaper rate. The selection of reds was probably the best in VN as was the price and yes, most enjoyable. You are strictly paying for the experience and a time gone by of French colonialism. To the owner I would say yes its nice to be exclusive, but at what cost " how many return customers?". Labour is cheap ($40 to 50 per month) most ingredients similarly cheap. Cut your prices by half at least, patronage should treble or more, the atmosphere will come alive and profits will up, up.... 
In VN when in doubt about an eating venue just observe and note the patronage. The locals are excellent judges.

Great Food, Great Service, Great Atmosphere!
Jun 2012 • Couples
I made a booking at La Villa about 2 weeks before i was due to arrive with my partner. It was meant to be a surprise for her as it was our anniversary weekend. 

Though the cab journey in was quite confusing as the taxi driver lost his way a couple of times, we eventually found the property - Right in the middle of the Villa District and surrounded by equally impressive villas around. Amazingly, there was a lady awaiting our arrival at the entrance to the beautiful and tastefully illuminated compound. I was evenmore surprised when she greeted me by name and ushered us to our table. Although i requested for a pool side table, they were kind enough to explain to me that due to the rain prior in the day and evening, they had to shift me inside, which was nice too as they purposefully set up a table which had an excellent view of the Garden that was also tucked away in a nice intimate corner for me and my partner to have nice quiet conversations. 

The table had everything i had requested for, the flowers, the card, all prepared to my specifications which surprised and delighted my partner. 

Tina the manager came to our table to personally welcome us and provide us the menu for what was to be a gastronomical journey for the night. 

It was the very first time both me and my partner had French fine dining and what a way to get started on the beautiful french culinary arts.

The Executive chef even made an appearance to welcome us and serve us tasty and appetizing canapes to whet the appetite. 

Though i cannot remember the names of the dishes we had that night, i clearly remember that my Australian Angus Beef was something that truly blew my mind away, while my partner's grilled sea bass with pasta was equally as delightful and delicious. 

The end off the night, the restaurant went a step further to write "Happy Anniversary" on our dessert plates as they were served. This really brought a big smile to my partner's face and seeing the way her eyes lit up warmed my heart. The desserts served were exquisite and the orange liquer they served us along with the Tea made it a real fine way to end the night. 

As we left the restaurant, it was a real pleasure to have the Executive Chef walk us out of the property. 

La Villa truly and deservedly, deserve the #1 spot on TripAdvisor. Kudos and Merci Beaucoup for a wonderful night at your restaurant La Villa!

jxdfjlsdjfklsdjlfs
Melbourne, Australia1 contribution
0
This place is probably one of the best-value restaurants in HCMC and a must try!
Jun 2012 • Friends
This restaurant is some distance from district 1 - it took us 20 minutes to get here in heavy traffic and about 10 minutes later in the evening on the way back. It is located in District 2 - an area popular with expats (as is District 7). The location and ambiance - a small, but immaculately presented villa/house on a quiet street. Lighting, decor and music for the indoor dining area was thought out.

We were presented with the special before the chef came to our table to take our orders. I really appreciated the time taken by him to answer my questions and explain the different menu items that neither my guest nor I were very familiar with. We decided to try his special for the evening - spatchcock. I had the soup with langoustine to start, then the pan fried sea bass and pasta next, followed by the spatchcock. For my desert, I took his recommendation for the apple tart. 

As we sat down, the amuse bouche arrived. Typical baked goodies, very delicious and made me really look forward to the starter.

I was apprehensive at first, going for shell fish, but the langoustine was presented with some of the shell taken off and I didn't have to work very hard for my food. The soup had delicate flavours that complimented the subtle flavours of the langoustine. 

The seabass was really good! The skin was crispy, and the fish not dry. The pasta was not mushy and not hard - al dente! It was really GOOD!

We shared the spatchcock, it was also very good. However, the portion was very large and we were unable to finish it. It came with vegetables cooked in the same stock as the spatchcock and was really tasty. I almost liked it more than the spatchcock.

The next course was the cheese. It was as expected. My palete isn't very sophisticated, so I probably didn't appreciate it. It tasted like a cheese platter should?

The final course was the apple tart, it was definitely the highlight. The pastry was very flakey and was exactly as the chef had described it. It came with delicious ice cream on top - I want to say it was rum and raisens, but I can't be sure. By this stage I was overly full, almost uncomfortable, but I couldn't help myself by finish every last bite of this dessert. 

I will definitely come back here if I come back to HCMC. It was tremendous value - only about $60AUD per head. Great value considering the ingredients and technique. I couldn't get this kind of value back in Melbourne.

I do however have two criticisms. 

1. I was offended when the male waiter took away my plates, as well as my guest's plate with the spatchcook while she was still eating her vegetables.

2. The portions are very large. I think with the MENU DE LA VILLA GOURMET, as it comes with two mains - these mains should be maybe smaller.

Thank you for an experience I will remember.

Well executed food with great flavour and balanced flavours and texteure. Pleasant efficient service in a lovely setting.

amazing food

Enjoyed the 5 course menu dinner. Well worth the price. The chef is a really nice guy, and has a really extensive menu, and really great food. The setting is superb - we had a table outside by the pool. and had fans around us, and some mosquito repellent on the table. 
Both of us really enjoyed our courses - except for the cheese. We found the camembert and the blue (?gorgonzola) much too salty. And felt like having bread as the accompaniment too heavy - crackers would have been a bit better, as we were feeling pretty full after our 3rd course. The feta mousse thing with truffle was a bit rich - but it is probably because we found the truffle flavour too strong (maybe we're not that fancy after all!), not because it was a bad dish. 
The chocoate mousse cake was delightful, as was the apricot sorbet. The flavour of the duck was really good - maybe a little bit on the rare side, (I asked for medium - medium rare). The lobster was great!!! Small touches such as the amuse bouche and the dessert plate at the end were appreciated. Service on the whole was really efficient and pleasant - maybe a bit too efficient, as they cleared away my partner's plate while I was still eating. 
Just one minor point - the water offered is Evian - which for us was just a bit too pricey. Maybe it would be nice to have a cheaper alternative (since it's $120,000 VND for a bottle?) since customers are already spending a whole lot more money on the food and wine?

We truly enjoyed ourselves - High end, great tasting French cuisine.
Mar 2012
Had to write the review immediately after dinner tonight. I brought my boyfriend there based on the recommendations from previous reviewers, I just have to say, "Merci beaucoup". Villa was set in a residential area of district 2. Beautiful villa with tall columns. Intimate garden setting and it was a good sized pool.

We booked through the conceirge of our hotel, Park Hyatt Saigon. We were given the address "La Villa Blanche" and apparently it meant the same, cos we were brought to the doorsteps of La Villa French Restaurant. Tina (Thierry's wife) was at the door to welcome us and we were shown to our table facing the pool, on the right hand side of the villa. My boyfriends deems it as the "high roller's" table. ;) my only suggestion is that a third fan be brought out for the corner tables as the two existing fans only catered to the needs of guests seated in the garden. 

Thierry came out to speak with us and gave us wonderful suggestions on what to order. Boyfriend ordered the "calamari ravioles" and I had the "pistou soup" to start. The ravioles were different in a good way and we could taste the sweetness of the calamari. My pistous soup came with the big prawn and the vegetable soup was refreshing, prawn succulent, sweet and cooked to perfection.

For main courses, I would definitely recommend the duck breast. The skin was crispy and the breast still pink and juicy. One of the best duck breast vie had ever. Boyfriend had the lamb tenderloin and our only complaint is there isn't enough lamb!! We had a bottle of white wine, and although we aren't dessert folks, the dessert was definitely worth the try. 

After reading the reviews, I have to stress that La Villa French is definitely high end for Vietnamese standards, but for the standard of French cuisine, i feel this is creme de la creme. 

Ps: Thierry knew his wine and the temperature to serve them at. Boyfriend has certain expectations of the temperature of white wine and the amount of wine to be served. Thierry's attention to perfection, is impeccable. Tina was warm and hospitable and I am so happy we went there for dinner on our last mightily HCMC. Kudos to Thierry, Godpapa, Tina and the team @ La Villa French. Manifique!

wonderful french food in ho chi minh city!!!!
Mar 2012
Having lived in ho chi minh city for the past 4 years it is a pleasure to have such an authentic french restaurant available as a change of culinary taste is often welcome. The restaurant has been open for 1 year, I am sorry that I discovered it a few months ago. Now it is a regular establishment for us to eat at least 3-4 times monthly for lunches as well as dinner. The restaurant is only a 15-20 minute car ride from district 1 now that the tunnel is open. It is located on a quite lane in district 2. upon arriving we are always warmly welcomed at the gate by the owners wife Tina who is most gracious and always smiling. Our table is always available and beautifully set up with flowers on the table. There is always a choice of sitting outside by the pool under umbrellas (fans are set up to keep you cool) for casual dining or inside for a fine dining experience. The staff is always attentive. Having now eaten there more than 15 times the reason we keep going back is because of Thierry. He is an exceptional owner/chef who takes his craft very seriously. He meets with each of the tables individually trying to understand the likes and dislikes of the patronage always trying to narrow down the menu to a choice of what that person would love to eat. The selections from starters, entrees ,main courses and desserts are changing as the seasons change. Thierry is only using the freshest ingredients in all that he prepares. By this time I have eaten most of the choices on the menu. The standouts are the calamari ravioli, brandade, roasted sturgeon, phan thiet lobster, st honore and mille feuille. That isn’t to say the other selections aren’t sensational too.
It is a must, for those that are travelling through ho chi minh city and for those living here, a welcome change.

Fantastic service and good food.
Feb 2012
My partner and I ate here for a special occassion and emailed a few weeks before to reserve a nice table. We got a quick response from the manager saying that we had a table by the pool reserved for us. The email even came with directions and a map to the restaurant so if you book via their website it's quick, easy and convenient.

However, when we got there, we weren't seated outside but instead next to the staircase. It wasn't what I expected but they said they moved us inside due to the wind and drizzling rain that happened a few hours before. We ended up moving outside and it was just right, the temperature was balmy and it wasn't too windy at all. After this minor issue the night went well. We ordered a small menu and a gourmet menu. The food was tasty, well executed and presented but it wasn't hugely exciting fine dining. I thought the best dishes were the foie gras terrine, duck and dark chocolate cake. It was expensive for Vietnam but compared to Australia, it was very cheap ($150USD a couple with starter drinks, bottle of wine, and set meals - lots of amuse bouche too). 

The chef/owner comes and talks to you to explain a few things if you need clarification too. Go for a special occassion if you feel like experiencing clean French flavours and exceptional service!

Ben_overthesea
Addis Ababa, Ethiopia4 contributions
0
Personal service and wonderful food
Feb 2012
This venue is a little bit of a ride from District 1 but worth taking the time for a special night out. Upon arriving you'll immediately get a feel for the place, it's a very homely (but stately) villa, as the name suggests. The staff will greet you warmly and be helpful throughout the night with menu suggestions.

My fiance and I enjoyed the four course menu (entree, main course, cheese plate and dessert). The selection of dishes is not overwhelming in variety but you feel as though you would like to try every single one. I know when I go back to Ho Chi Minh City I will visit again and experience the menu further! I would like to give a special mention to the pesto vegetable soup with langoustine, it was superb! This soup had a very hearty texture which was unexpected for something mainly made with vegetables, and was a perfect entree. My fiance commends the chef on her main course selection, which was the duck with morel sauce.

We have no experience with French wines, and so allowed the staff to select one for us. They chose well! I'd also like to suggest the limoncello as a digestif, which was lovely! Apparently it is a house recipe.

I found the pricing of the food to be acceptable. In Ho Chi Minh City you can, of course, find very cheap restaurants and eat for little money. But this is not an everyday restaurant, and for the fine dining experience you get it is well worth the price. Unlike some fine dining restaurants you actually get a good amount of food on the plate and it is unlikely you'll leave feeling hungry. A comparable dining experience in Australia would cost us a great deal more than what we paid at La Villa!

Thanks to Chef Thierry and the maître d’hôtel Tina for a night with good food, good service, and lovely atmosphere!

From Ben and Tham.

New Year's Bonanza
Dec 2011
We booked well in advance to celebrate New Year's at La Villa with their special set New Year's Menu. The three of us had really looked forward to this evening as a highlight of our vacation in Vietnam, and we were not disappointed!

Upon booking however they requested a deposit and wanted us to send them copies of our credit card. We felt a bit uneasy about this and asked for alternative means of paying this deposit. Unfortunately it was not possible to use for example PayPal, but they instead let us come by the restaurant once we got to Saigon and pay the deposit in cash. The chef, Thierry, greeted us and sat down with us to present the menu for the upcoming dinner which of course further raised our expectations.

On the night we were treated exceptionally well from getting out of the taxi up until we left the restaurant four hours later. Thierry and his crew really delivered and made our night special. The food was delicious (especially the lobster with strawberries which was to die for) and plentiful. Full of interesting flavors and visual wonders, this is a restaurant with ambition that takes dining in Saigon to a different level. 

Towards the end of the dinner Thierry emerged from the kitchen and walked around all the tables to make sure that we were all satisfied and had a good time, and as others have pointed out he also made sure to shake hands with all parties before they left the restaurant. A nice gesture indeed. 

Did we not have anything to complain about? Well, not really, but we raised our eyebrows slightly when we realized La Villa only served imported water from France. We should have appreciated at least the option to choose local, shipping water all the way from Europe is just ridiculous. 

We would definitely go back and try the normal menu and highly recommend this restaurant. Hopefully Thierry repeats the New Year's dinner next year so that you can try it out for yourself!

Looking forward to visiting Saigon and eat again in your home soon.
Nov 2011
After a long trip in Vietnam, I was extremely happy from my Hotel concierge recommendation.
This on says: "this is not in the city center, but it's worth the trip" 
In fact the trip was reasonable less than 15mins to arrive at the villa. 
Warm welcome from the taxi door by a charming Vietnamese lady. Big smile, caring... ( I understand later that she was the Chef's wife). 
We had a nice table in the garden. Candles everywhere, which created a beautiful and romantic ambiance.
The Chef came out from the kitchen to greet us, Originally from south of France (with a tipical French accent, he introduce us his menu, also his philosophy and the villa concept) describe as a family business, uncle doing the pastry, his wife to take care of the service...)
I make my choice for a Brandade follow by a rack of Lamb. 
My partner ordered the foie Gras, then the parmigiano ravioli. 
We ordered a bottle of Clos des Fees. actually I was surprised to find such a good wine coming from a boutique winery on the list, in fact the winemaker of this wine use to be one of France best Sommelier, and the wine itself is becoming one of the best wine from South of France. 
The dishes were perfectly executed, the brandade has the same taste than in France, the foie gras terrine was well cooked an seasoned exactly as we liked it. 
The lamb was cooked as I request it, tender, flavory... Even if my friend has the very small appetite, she finished all the ravioli without giving me the chance to try, she even deep her bread in the sauce, leaving the plate clean. 
If this is not a sign, In 4 years I never saw her doing this, even at the caprice in HK or Le chateaubriand in Paris.
She told me later on our way back to the Hotel, that she done this because she was feeling like home. 
And it is true The chef and his wife have created a place were we actually feel well...
Mr Thierry and Tina, Thank yu, Looking forward to visiting Saigon and eat again in your home soon.

Disappointed
Oct 2011
It's a pity I had to give a 3 rating to La Villa even though service was truly impeccable. The owner welcomed & shook hands with each patron enthusiastically and dashed out from his busy kitchen to say goodbye to each of them when they left. The wait staff was very attentive, they got a taxi waiting for us at the front door when we departed without our asking. Service was definitely 5+ but unfortunately our food last night was below our expectation. We had planned to pick from the a la carte menu but then the owner came and recommended his special dish of the night (Bouillabaisse) most fervently & zealously. He said we would have a fish soup for starter, then 4 kinds of fishes for the main, plus a dessert (not on the menu) made from his creativity that night. I ordered the Bouillabaisse at the owner’s repeated assurances of excellence. My husband was about to order from the main menu but then the owner said he couldn’t do the Bouillabaisse for 1 person, so both of us ended up ordering the same thing. We have tried Bouillabaisse many times before, both in France and outside of France. The fish soup (starter) we had last night was good, but it was just as good as the other good ones we had before, nothing extraordinary. Guess our disappointment lied mostly with the main entrée. It was basically 3 pieces of fish plus scallops, all covered in the SAME fish soup which we had as a starter. The presentation of the entrée was not aesthetically pleasant to the eye, to be exact, there was no “presentation” at all. Flavor-wise, it was like eating chunks of fish served in a “Bouillabaisse dressing”, not very exciting. Technically, it was one dish split into two and we were not too thrilled about it. We understand that sometimes it could be your bad day and you order the wrong stuff and have a not-so-satisfying meal, so be it. But what we didn’t understand was that why this particular Bouillabaisse could only be ordered at a minimum of 2 persons when we could always order much-more-elaborate-looking Bouillabaisse singly in France? If we had ordered just one Bouillabaisse, at least the other person would have an opportunity to try out other dishes in the main menu and cut down our disappointment by half. After all, La Villa is quite a way from city center and we came all the way anticipating a night of indulgence (after reading all the great reviews). Anyway, the complimentary amuse-bouches tasted great and our dessert was also very good.

Authentic french - great flavours, exquisitely presented at a surprisingly reasonable price
Sep 2011
We went to La Villa for someone special's birthday while in HCMC, as a bit of a treat. It's probably a special occasion sort of place, which all but the low prices would support.
Thierry was out there doing his best to make us feel at home, discussing the menu and agreeing that the least expensive fixed price option was probably all we needed. It consisted of three courses from the a la carte menu (with one or two exclusions) and cost around $30 per person.
We had scallops and diced pork entrees, followed by lamb and duck. All beautifully presented, using fine ingredients from around the Pacific. Servings were quite adequate but not excessive. Desserts were delicate and delicious.
Drinks started with a glass each of champagne, a mid-range bottle of French Shiraz (the wine menu is pretty much all French, but Thierry recommended well to suit our meal), followed by Armagnac with our coffees. The night was peppered with amuse bouche morsels.
Staff were skilled and attentive.
Overall cost was around $200, but the drink choices accounted for 2/3 of that amount. At home, this quality of French cooking would command over double the price.

Exceptional - a must to visit in Ho Chi Minh
Aug 2011
We booked dinner at La Villa on the day of our arrival in Ho Chi Minh upon TA's reviews. We were impressed from the moment we made the telephone reservation as the staff was helpful, friendly and spoke good English. When we arrived at the restaurant, we were warmly welcomed. We were given amuse bouche whilst we perused the menu. The owner (Thierry) came to welcome us and answer any questions we had on the items on the menu. I took the La Petite set menu which is a 3 course menue (starter, main and dessert) whilst my spouse took the La Villa set menue which had an extra cheese course. WIth the help of Thierry, we made our selections and every course, ranged from very good to exceptional. Whilst the service staff's English was limited, they were eager to please and kept our glasses of water filled and offered us the wonderful baguettes and rolls throughout the meal. We had a delicious and thoroughly enjoyable and relaxing dinner ending with some complimentary after dinner biscuits/pastries. The staff called for a taxi when we were ready to leave and Thierry came to walk us out to the taxi. The next few days' meals paled in comparison with La Villa's so much so that we decided to go back for lunch 3 days later on our last day in Ho Chi Minh. Thierry recognised us and as ever, the food and service was incredible. The restaurant is a little ways out of the main city (15 minutes by taxi) but if not for that, I am sure that La Villa would be packed to the rafters in view of the quality and value of the food and the excellent service. In any case, I would highly recommend everyone to take the effort to eat at La Villa as you will be well rewarded. This will be at the very top of "must visit" places in Ho Chi Minh from now on.

Very good indeed. The best restaurant in HCM? Probably.
Jun 2011
We went to La Villa for dinner recently. Disappointingly our e-mail for a reservation went unanswered but we can perhaps put this down to teething problems as the restaurant is quite new. Although it is a little off the beaten track it is only $6 and 15 minutes in a cab. This should not put you off in any way. Unfortunately there was a storm when we arrived and so we had to sit inside. The outside tables in the beautiful garden looked better to my eye.

I have struggled slightly with how to contextualise this review so as not to be misunderstood. I have decided to judge it by the standards that I would judge a London or New York restaurant rather than one in Ho Chi Minh, by which I mean by HCM standards La Villa is exceptional. If you want a top notch splurge meal then there is probably only one place to go in HCM. I’m not sure that the restaurant is quite at Michelin Star standard yet, but the menu is certainly very well put together, and is just let down slightly by the execution of some of the dishes.

No review of La Villa can pass without reference to the most convivial of hosts Msr Mounon who should be congratulated for taking on the task of bringing fine dining to HCM. He enhanced our enjoyment of the restaurant with the knowledge and provenance he brought to the menu, and his fine recommendation of an eclectic bottle of wine which we shall seek out on our return home. And, due to a mix up in our ordering he was more than reasonable in knocking a sizable chunk from the bill!

The cuisine is French and the menu is diverse, well constructed and interesting with the meal preceded by an amuse bouche. All of the food was very tasty. Presentation was faultless, and the service as mentioned above excellent. If I was being critical my sturgeon was probably a minute over cooked, and the risotto on which it sat slightly stodgy. To repeat though, this really is picking fault. 

La Villa has only been open for 3/4 months and you can see on Trip Advisor that it has been very well received. Msr Mounon commented that the local patronage is not what he would like. They really should give it a try, and a better website would help to promote the business. 

We very much enjoyed our meal at La Villa. We would certainly go back. By the standards of the West it is an absolute bargain at c$35-40 a head (excl. wine). The location is beautiful, the service very good, the host a wonderful benefit to the business, and the food and wine of excellent quality. The best meal in HCM? Almost certainly.

A Place for a Special Occasion
May 2011
So it was our last night in Saigon, after a week long holiday in Vietnam and we wanted to have our last dinner at some place special. Figuring that Vietnam should have some great French Restaurant around (being a former French colony), trip advisor brought as to La Villa.

Ambience
La Villa is situated in a quiet neighbourhood in District 2, definitely a great retreat from the noise, dust and hectic craziness of the city. Passing by the high walled houses on the way in to the restaurant, we were in for something special upon reaching the impressive gates. Like the home of a rich relative and yet warm and embracing that you certainly feel like an honoured guest of Monsieur Thierry!

Al Fresco dining by the swimming pool with a deco that demands photographs. The inside of the house was in the style of a French Manor. Immediately, we had the owner of the house and chef of the restaurant, Thierry, welcome us with a sensitivity that could only come from years of experience - we originally chose a spot near a huge table till Thierry recommended that we sit at the other side of the room so that we would not be disturbed by the noise that the soon to arrive huge-table-group would be making. He was proven correct. 

The cosiness of the place and the lighting definitely gave a great ambience although softer French ballads might have put us more in the mood for a night of fine wine and great cooking!

The Food
The bread (Brown bread, olive, tomato, baguette) , probably fresh from the kitchen was light and went well with the olive oil and butter. 

The hors d'œuvre was a delightful pastry (with 3 different kinds of toppings) that was followed by a shot of clam soup that was really one of the best I've ever tasted.

For the entrée, we ordered a Ravoli, scallops, a pork and pig lever combination and crab bisque. As we passed around the dishes (totally not in fine dining style) all four of us remarked that they were really good. Definitely an A+ in my standard. The blend of flavours, the texture and presentation was top marks. 

With great expectancy, we awaited the main course. We took the lamb rack, the steak done medium-rare to medium, the monkfish and scallops. All of these were paired with something tasty, steak with steak fries, monkfish with risotto, lamb with ratatouille, and monkfish on a blend of vegetables. The sauces were good, but we felt a little let down by the meats. While the scallops were smooth and tender, the steak had a very strong flavour to it, the lamb could have been tenderer and the monkfish, a little wetter. 

I gently remarked that perhaps we Singaporeans are spoilt when it comes to the mains (with Mortons of Chicago for steak for comparison). However to be fair, we didn't try the house speciality, which would be the lobster. 

However, the desserts were once again fantastic. Can't quite remember the French names, but the chocolate cake was really really good (very chocolaty), the apple crumble was warm and had a bite to it, the caramel treacle with cream puffs was very unique and my cake with a biscuit base with cream and an icing top was lovely. Not forgetting the caramel icecream that came with all the desserts.

Total Damage done: 2,990,000 dong (inclusive of 4 set dinners, 2 glasses of wine, 1 latte and 1 bottle of Evian) which works out to a very affordable USD 36.50 per person. For such service and dining experience, one would expect to pay at least double the price in Singapore or the US.

For a 3.5 months old restaurant, I have to say that La Villa will be around for a very long time! 

(And yes, we were dressed very touristy-causally!)

Good French food, excellent host
La Villa is about 15 minutes out of Ho Vhi Minh set in at the garden of a private house. The night we went was quite quiet, just after a local long weekend, but we would have been happy the if it was just us. As it happens there was one other table. The owner Thierry looked after us impeccably and left us wanting for little. He was very informative about every aspect of the menu, we're quite foody, and was quick to answer any questions and offer recommendations. The extensive wine list included some new ones for us and Thierry suggested a truly delicious 2007 St. Joseph (420 Nuits), which despite the dodgy name, was perfect for the warm evening air and rich food. Speaking of which, we ordered; Crab Bisque - rich, bursting with deep crab flavor / Calamari raviole - deliciously light but could be hotter / Cote de beouf - was well cooked but needed something to lift it above standard fare / Magret du canard - excellent. The best I've had. Tender, succulent, meaty and with served with a sauce (although I forget exactly what it was) that just picked it up beautifully. Dessert was the chocolate Concorde - excellent and the mille-feuille - again very good. Our first foray into French food in Ho Chi Minh and overall, a very good experience. Go for a table outside, the inside needs a bit of atmosphere but perhaps a busier night provides that. Bravo Thierry!

Good overall, but overpriced and in the wrong location for the concept
Mar 2011
Whilst the proprietors and the staff are charming and the villa setting is beautiful, there are a few fundamental mistakes here IMHO. 

Firstly, the prices are too high and they are quoted in USD on the menu which is not only impolite, but illegal in Vietnam. Secondly, while I have no problem whatsoever with a short menu there should be an acknowledgment that vegetarians and kids exist (I took both on my visit). Thirdly, I think they have overdone the fine dining element in a suburban area where the primary audience is families. I wonder whether tourists and businesspeople from the city will cross the bridge to visit an upscale French Restaurant and I would also question whether the residents of An Phu will go to a local restaurant for a fine dining meal instead of going "into town" for a night out at a good French restaurant. 

On the positive side, the dishes are creatively conceived and in general well executed (although my wife's scallops were chewy and tasteless). The provision of amuse-bouches and lots of good fresh bread was generous and perhaps in some way made up for the high prices. The service staff were well trained and attentive, but looked preposterous in a tropical alfresco environment in their business suits, ties and scarves. 

All in all this might be a once-a-year-for-something-a-bit-different place for us, whereas if the menu was more accessible and the prices were better, I would be there with the family at least a couple of times a month.
